# Tool Registry

Tracks researched tools. Check before first use, update after research.

| Tool | Version | Date | Key Learnings |
|------|---------|------|---------------|
| faster-whisper / CTranslate2 / PyAV | 1.2.1 / 4.9.0 / 19.0.2 | 2026-11-12 | Local GPU transcription lives in `devops/transcription`. Pin model snapshots by exact Hugging Face commit and retain tokenizer files to prevent unpinned fallback downloads. Use native sequential decoding with context and standard temperature fallback; no VAD trimming by default. Set and record the initial native seed before CUDA/model workers initialize: CTranslate2 caches RNGs per thread, so a later global seed reset does not reset reused workers. Sampling fallback can reset prior-text context and introduce bidi formatting even when its compression heuristic rejects fluent Hebrew. Strip Unicode Bidi_Control only from derived HTML, preserve raw recognition and all Hebrew letters, and use the CPU-only `transcription:compare` task for direction-aware edit distances. Invisible U+202B controls inflated one lecture pair from 4.90% readable word disagreement to 17.22%; neither percentage is a reference-based accuracy score. Beam-only replay is explicit, and larger beams require accuracy evidence. PyAV directly decodes the explicitly selected audio stream to mono float32 16 kHz and flushes the resampler tail; upstream faster-whisper's decoder skips invalid frames, so the quality-focused pipeline owns strict decoding. Multiple audio streams require explicit selection. ASR timestamp overlaps/overruns are raw review diagnostics, not proof that recognized text is invalid. CUDA 12 requires compatible cuBLAS/cuDNN 9 libraries; the Windows CT2 wheel preloads a bundled cuDNN dispatcher, so installed package versions alone do not establish loaded DLL versions. Arrange an explicitly authorized exclusive GPU window and record every compute PID throughout representative tests: concurrent LLM allocations can cause Windows shared-memory paging and confound capacity/timing conclusions. Exclusive FP32 long-form decoding can also exceed an 8 GiB GPU: the representative 24.37-minute lecture completed with explicit FP16 in 15.11 minutes (1.61 track minutes/runtime minute), retaining the full model and search settings; its full WebM counterpart completed in 12.51 minutes (1.95 track minutes/runtime minute). A short FP32 smoke does not establish full-lecture memory capacity, and cross-precision text agreement is not an accuracy/WER result. [Backend](https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper), [PyAV](https://pyav.basswood-io.com/docs/stable/api/audio.html). |
| Plugin.Firebase.Auth / Plugin.Firebase.Firestore | 5.0.1 / 4.0.0 | 2026-11-05 | Android/iOS only — reference the packages inside a `GetTargetPlatformIdentifier == 'ios' OR == 'android'` ItemGroup and guard call sites with `#if ANDROID \|\| IOS` (matches the existing Plugin.Firebase.Analytics pattern); MacCatalyst/Windows are unsupported. `CrossFirebaseAuth.Current` throws when the native app was never configured, so resolve it lazily (after the iOS init lifecycle callback) behind a try boundary. Auth surface: `CurrentUser?.Uid`, `SignInAnonymouslyAsync()`, `AddAuthStateListener(Action<FirebaseUser?>)` returning a disposable. Firestore surface: `CrossFirebaseFirestore.Current.GetDocument("users/{uid}")` → `GetDocumentSnapshotAsync<Dictionary<string, object>>()` / `SetDataAsync(IDictionary)` — read/write plain dictionaries (no reflection DTOs) to stay AOT-safe; snapshot `.Data` is `IDictionary` on Android (not `IReadOnlyDictionary<string,object?>`), so accept `System.Collections.IDictionary` in the codec. The Firestore SDK queues writes offline and retries itself. [Repo](https://github.com/TobiasBuchholz/Plugin.Firebase). |
| Local Tanahpedia GPU inference | torch 2.14.1+cu126 / transformers 5.22.2 | 2026-11-11 | RTX 4070 Laptop 8 GiB + NVIDIA 566.07 runs CUDA 12.6. The cu126 index has no torch 2.15.0 wheel; use the separately pinned annotation CUDA profile rather than installing a newer incompatible runtime. Explicit device/dtype validation, TF32-off FP32 comparison, safetensors and immutable model revisions keep qualification reproducible. Classifier and generative inference remain offline; generation writes local row files. [PyTorch wheel matrix](https://pytorch.org/get-started/previous-versions/). |
| Local Tanahpedia CPU inference | torch 2.15.0+cpu / transformers 5.22.2 | 2026-11-13 | Use the separate official CPU wheel. Windows CPU inference in the 2.14.1+cu126 build produced native access violations; eager attention was not reliable, so no attention override was retained. The CPU-only profile completed both curated splits with counts, metrics, per-case and per-category results identical to GPU FP32. The loader rejects the known crashing Windows/CUDA-wheel/CPU combination before weights load. CUDA inference keeps its tested driver-compatible profile. [CPU requirements](../data/annotations/requirements-encoders.txt). |
| Hugging Face structured decoding | lm-format-enforcer 0.11.3 / transformers 5.22.2 | 2026-11-11 | LMFE's bundled adapter imports `PreTrainedTokenizerBase` from a removed path; the local minimal MIT core bridge avoids package/global patches. `TokenEnforcer` also replaces `parser.config`: restore the explicit Unicode alphabet, whitespace and field-order policy afterward. Real pinned DictaLM/Qwen tokenizer tests validate Hebrew diacritics and emoji. Use source-index enums because integer minimum/maximum are not enforced. Code derives source surfaces from validated indices; model output never rewrites text. [Pinned upstream integration](https://github.com/noamgat/lm-format-enforcer/blob/v0.11.3/lmformatenforcer/integrations/transformers.py). |
| Hugging Face model prefetch | huggingface-hub 2.4.0 / hf_xet 1.8.0 | 2026-11-11 | Prefetch the pinned model's tokenizer and official chat template as well as safetensors; some snapshots use `chat_template.jinja`. For observed Xet stalls with many TLS connections, bounded `HF_XET_AC_MAX_DOWNLOAD_CONCURRENCY=4`, `HF_XET_HIGH_PERFORMANCE=0` and one file worker restored progress; verify progress rather than extending timeouts. | actions/download-artifact | v8 (9000827) | 2026-11-02 | A `pattern` that matches exactly one artifact extracts it straight into `path`; only two or more matches get per-artifact subdirectories (`isSingleArtifactDownload \|\| mergeMultiple \|\| artifacts.length === 1` in [src/download-artifact.ts](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/blob/9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333/src/download-artifact.ts)). Consumers that locate artifacts by subdirectory name must handle the flat single-match layout (the single-shard iOS merge in `merge-runner-shards.mjs`). Artifacts consumed by `needs` jobs must outlive a failed-job re-run: a 1-day plan artifact made a re-run merge fail with `Artifact not found`. |
| web-push | 4.0.0 | 2026-11-08 | Node Web Push sender (VAPID JWT + RFC 8291 aes128gcm payload encryption). v4 is ESM-only (`"type": "module"`) with named exports only — no default export; import `{ sendNotification, setVapidDetails, WebPushError }` directly. Call `setVapidDetails(subject, publicKey, privateKey)` once, then `sendNotification(subscription, payload, { TTL, topic, urgency })`; `topic` must be <= 32 URL-safe chars and replaces an undelivered message with the same topic. Failures throw `WebPushError` with `statusCode`: 404/410 mean the subscription is gone and should be deleted. Ships no bundled types; `@types/web-push@3.6.x` still matches the named-export surface. Jest's CommonJS runtime cannot `require()` it — `jest.mock("web-push", factory)` in every test file that loads a module importing it (e.g. via `requireActual`). Browsers: Chromium/Opera/Samsung use `fcm.googleapis.com`, Firefox `updates.push.services.mozilla.com`, Edge on Windows `*.notify.windows.com`, Safari/iOS 16.4+ (installed web app only) `web.push.apple.com`. Safari needs `applicationServerKey` as bytes, not the base64url string. `bunx web-push generate-vapid-keys` makes the key pair. [Next.js PWA guide](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/progressive-web-apps). |
| Appium `wdaConnectionTimeout` | appium-webdriveragent 16.13.6 | 2026-10-06 | The capability is the `WebDriverProxy` per-request timeout applied to every proxied WDA command, including `POST /session` during session creation — not just the initial connection. A cold app launch can exceed 90 s and fail with "Unable to start WebDriverAgent session ... timeout of 90000ms exceeded". Keep the xcuitest driver default of 240 s (inside the client's five-minute session budget). `wdaStartupRetries: 1` deliberately disables xcuitest's startup retry loop, so this timeout is the only startup margin. |
| git-filter-repo | 2.47.0 | 2026-10-06 | `pip install --user git-filter-repo`; on Windows invoke the exe under `%APPDATA%\Python\Python312\Scripts` directly since it is not on PATH. Run on a fresh `git clone --mirror`; `--invert-paths --paths-from-file` strips paths across all refs including tags. Old objects stay in the pack until `reflog expire --expire=now --all` + `gc --prune=now`, so measure `size-pack` only after GC. Stripping this repo's generated dumps took the pack from 395 MB to ~15 MB. |
| git lfs migrate | git-lfs 3.7.1 | 2026-10-06 | `git lfs migrate import --everything --include=<globs>` rewrites every ref, converts matched blobs to LFS pointers, and appends LFS rules to `.gitattributes` in the rewritten commits. GitHub bills LFS to the repo owner: storage counts every migrated historical version (1 GB free), and each clone checkout downloads that revision's objects (1 GB/mo free); `actions/checkout` defaults to `lfs: false` and fetches pointers only. Migrating this repo's dumps produced a 9 MB pack with a 1.9 GB LFS store. |
| Appium read-only text snapshots | Appium.WebDriver 9.0.0 / Selenium 4.52.0 | 2026-11-12 | [iOS shard failure](https://github.com/bible-on-site/bible-on-site/actions/runs/43186232566/job/131086331808) reproduced a lookup/read race: `WaitFor(...).Text` requested a recycled verse after the accepted snapshot. Capture read-only text inside the existing visibility condition; keep returned elements live for later actions and preserve native text, interaction deadlines and session-death handling. The `TestMobileE2EUnit` Nuke target exercises a fake native executor that throws on a later text request and returns fresh state on consecutive lookups. Both new cases fail before the fix; all 145 harness unit cases pass afterward. |
| Cold Appium reader snapshot | XCUITest 12.15.0 | 2026-10-05 | In [merge-queue run 37353901272](https://github.com/bible-on-site/bible-on-site/actions/runs/37353901272/job/111912697150), the first PerekSource lookup took 70 seconds and returned an empty loading-page snapshot; the reader appeared during that request and was visible in the failure diagnostics. | macOS sample | built-in macOS 26 command | 2026-10-05 | `sample <pid> 2 1 -mayDie -file <path>` records all native thread stacks for two seconds at 1 ms intervals. `-mayDie` preserves symbols when an automated app exits or crashes during collection; no UI is opened. Collect only after failed tests: background symbolication timed out and competed with healthy iOS sessions on CI. Allow two minutes for sampling and 30 seconds for process lookup. Startup checkpoints and fresh `.ips` reports locate the failing native transition when XCTest cannot retrieve the view tree. [Apple command manual](https://keith.github.io/xcode-man-pages/sample.1.html). |

| .NET Android R8 obfuscation | Microsoft.Android.Sdk 36.1.118 (workload set 10.0.402.1) | 2026-10-27 | `AndroidR8ObfuscationMode` (`disabled`|`private-members`) shipped in the .NET 10 servicing stream only from 36.1.118 — 36.1.69 and earlier silently inject `-dontobfuscate` and never emit `r8.json`, so the property is a no-op there; guard on `$(AndroidNETSdkVersion)` or fail. `private-members` switches R8 to `proguard-android-optimize.txt`, obfuscates private/package-private members, and keeps all class/interface names and public/protected members (the JNI/ACW surface in proguard_xamarin.cfg). The AAB carries `BUNDLE-METADATA/com.android.tools/r8.json` (`options.isObfuscationEnabled/isShrinkingEnabled/isOptimizationsEnabled`) and `com.android.tools.build.obfuscation/proguard.map`; Play reads both from the uploaded bundle — no separate upload step exists. Play's 25% thresholds apply to apps over 10 MB uncompressed DEX from February 2027. Verify with `app/devops/verify_android_dex_metadata.py`. |
| GitHub Actions cancellation | workflow status conditions | 2026-10-05 | Aggregate jobs need `always() && !cancelled()` to evaluate test failures while releasing the PR concurrency slot when a newer head replaces the run. | NuGet dependency snapshots | component-detection action 0.2.0; dependency-review action 5 | 2026-10-06 | The SDK labels PR snapshots with the head SHA, while default checkout scans the synthetic merge. Match source and metadata; submit the actual merge base and head with a stable correlator; the API compares their common ancestor, not necessarily the current base tip. Version-only bases can also lack graphs. Preserve the exact required `submit-nuget` check in PR and queue contexts with failing aggregate gates; reusable/matrix check names are scoped. Use one nonempty `nuget` submission. Duplicating it under the historical job name changed 2/1 snapshot counts to 3/2 without repairing the comparison; remove that ineffective trial. The review action can pass after its retry timeout with snapshot warnings still present. The guard remains a draft pending [GitHub historical snapshot repair](https://github.com/bible-on-site/bible-on-site/issues/2002). The supported API does not list/filter/delete historical identities. Queue/master ref duplication is unproven; do not pad counters or forge metadata. Use the named `test:dependency-snapshots`/`verify:dependency-snapshots` devops tasks; inspect reusable submission job logs directly. [Submission inputs](https://github.com/advanced-security/component-detection-dependency-submission-action/blob/v0.2.0/action.yml), [review inputs](https://github.com/actions/dependency-review-action/blob/v5/action.yml), [comparison API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/dependency-graph/dependency-review). |

| Bun install scripts | 1.4.4 | 2026-10-26 | Dependency lifecycle scripts run only for names in `package.json` `trustedDependencies` (bun's equivalent of pnpm `allowBuilds`, not a bunfig key); blocked scripts print a warning rather than hard-fail. `bunfig.toml [install]`: `linker = "hoisted"` reproduces npm's flat node_modules (`isolated` is the pnpm-like default for workspaces), `exact = true` pins saved ranges, `minimumReleaseAge` is seconds (86400 = pnpm's 1440min default) with `minimumReleaseAgeExcludes`. Overrides use npm syntax in `package.json` — nested `{"parent": {"child": "ver"}}` works under both bun and npm; pnpm's flat `"parent>child"` key breaks `npx`/`npm`. npm's `--prefix`/`-C` maps to per-subcommand `--cwd` (`bun install --cwd <dir>`, `bun run --cwd <dir>` — no global flag); `npm ci` to `bun install --frozen-lockfile`; `npx` to `bun x`. Windows `.bin` shims are `<name>.exe`+`<name>.bunx` (no `tsc.cmd`), so `npx` misses local bins — use `bun x`. Corepack does not manage bun: install locally via `npm i -g bun`, CI via `oven-sh/setup-bun@v2`, and Docker via `COPY --from=oven/bun:<ver>-alpine@sha256:...` (pin the digest for hadolint). bun.lock is text (JSONC); bun writes no `.modules.yaml`/`.package-lock.json` marker — use `node_modules/.bin` presence to detect a completed install. `actions/setup-node` `cache:` accepts only `npm|yarn|pnpm` — `cache: bun` fails at runtime (#2643); cache Bun's store via explicit `actions/cache` on `~/.bun/install/cache` and gate the enum with `devops/github/ci/setup-node-cache.mjs`. |

| Android emulator runner | 2.38.0 | 2026-10-05 | Linux CI uses KVM and an x86_64 API 36 image. Match the app RID to `android-x64` and embed assemblies in Debug APKs; Fast Deployment APKs cannot run on a fresh CI emulator. | Android AVD cache locks | emulator-runner 2.38.0 | 2026-10-28 | [Master run 40680777898](https://github.com/bible-on-site/bible-on-site/actions/runs/40680777898/job/122791950490) exited during snapshot-lock acquisition before any app test, then exhausted the unchanged boot deadline polling the absent device. [Upstream file locks](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/qemu/+/emu-master-dev/android/emu/files/src/android/utils/filelock.cpp) append `.lock` and store a host PID: a restored `snapshot.lock.lock` can collide with an unrelated live PID on the next runner. The failed artifact did not record its lock files, so that exact PID collision remains an inference. Treat root AVD `*.lock` entries as host state: inspect processes and ADB devices successfully, prove the selected AVD is offline, then log and remove only those locks before reuse and cache publication. Preserve payload, other AVDs and all boot/shutdown deadlines; fail closed on active or unknown ownership. Keep the existing cache key so CI exercises and diagnoses the suspect entry rather than hiding it behind a cache miss. |
| iOS boot identity handoff | Xcode 27; simctl | 2026-10-28 | [Master iOS shard 1](https://github.com/bible-on-site/bible-on-site/actions/runs/40680777898/job/122796530758) started its selected iPhone, then `ios:boot:wait` redundantly ran `simctl list devices available --json` and exhausted the existing 300-second command deadline with no output. The job had no restored simulator-cache hit, so do not attribute this to cached device corruption; the operating-system stall's cause is unproven. Pass start's successful `udid`/`version` outputs directly to wait, validate both against the SDK, and monitor that exact device with bootstatus and the native bridge. Standalone selection stays available; partial/invalid handoffs fail. Keep all deadlines and retain start/wait output in diagnostic artifacts. |
| Blocked API release selection | Node 26; GitHub published releases | 2026-10-28 | [Master CI 40680777898](https://github.com/bible-on-site/bible-on-site/actions/runs/40680777898) built and tested API 0.1.94 but skipped release after mobile startup failures. A CI-only followup's event diff does not select that API again; manual CI dispatch also cannot publish, while rerunning the old run retains its broken helpers. Reconcile only on otherwise API-unchanged master pushes against the latest published canonical API tag's immutable source. Ignore only the API's own Cargo versions, never dependency or source changes; version-only bumps remain no-ops. Select fresh API tests/build/release through unchanged quality/provenance gates, change no other module flags, and fail closed on metadata/fetch/version ambiguity. Reuse available baseline commits and preserve existing repository history depth: a depth-1 fetch in a full shared checkout changes history visibility across worktrees. New release-selection behavior requires the repository's specific AWS PR approval. |
|| adb incremental install | platform-tools >= 30.0.1 | 2026-10-29 | `adb install` silently picks an IncFS incremental install whenever the client binary (>= 30.0.1) and the device (`adb -s <udid> features` lists `abb_exec`) both support it — the same predicate appium-adb's `isIncrementalInstallSupported` uses. Xamarin mmaps `assemblies.blob` out of the staged APK and can SIGSEGV in libmonodroid `open_from_bundles` before IncFS materializes the page (#2773). UiAutomator2's AUT install path (`initAUT`/`installAUT`) has no incremental opt-out — `noIncremental` exists in appium-adb but is wired only for the uiautomator2 server APKs — so the pilot installs the app itself with `--no-incremental` and hands the session `noReset` (`MOBILE_APP_PREINSTALLED`), which skips `initAUT` entirely. `adb uninstall` exits nonzero on an absent package, so probe `pm path <pkg>` first. Parse the binary version from the `^Version x.y.z` line, not `Android Debug Bridge version` (that line is the 1.0.41 bridge protocol). |
